grades.quote: Note that although CSRs and instructions are associated with one privilege level, they are also accessible at all higher privilege levels.
grades.reason: Gives background that CSRs are accessible by a subset of privilege levels and are accessible at higher levels. It never says what happens when a lower-privilege access is attempted, such as an illegal-instruction exception.
Discusses a hypervisor using State Enable to trap guest accesses to Smctr/Ssctr state. It does not cover user-mode CSR access lacking privilege or the resulting exception.
Lists CSR address ranges and their read/write or read-only classes. It does not state the outcome of an access made without the required privilege.
Covers the MXR and SUM bits and their effect on memory access privilege. It has nothing to do with CSR access privilege checks.
